problem_statement: aross2010/web-portfolio is a polished Next.js 14 App Router personal portfolio for software engineer Alex Ross: a fixed top navbar, an intro/hero, a Top Skills icon grid, a Projects section, an Experience timeline, and a Connect contact form, rendered inside a centered max-w-[1000px] main column with Tailwind and framer-motion. The Projects section ships a project browser — a "Featured work" control whose row of discipline tabs (All / Mobile / AI · ML / Web / Systems, derived from the projects' own stacks) filters a card grid of Alex's six projects (Spotter, Heat Check, Duel, X/Twitter Bot Detector, Spotlefy, Additional Projects) and shows a live result count ("Showing 2 of 6 · Web"). The project browser is meant to stay continuous across the portfolio: its discipline tab row and count readout ride every primary route — the home page and the /resume and /pursuits routes — while the full card grid renders on the home route where the projects live. A recent change left the browser with several defects. LAYOUT (responsive): the discipline tab row is pinned to a fixed 640px width with flex-wrap:nowrap, so on a 390px phone the no-wrap tab row forces the document far wider than the viewport, producing a large horizontal scroll on every mobile state while desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) fit. LAYOUT (filtered grid): the filtered card grid is laid out with display:flex / flex-wrap:nowrap and each card pinned to a fixed 340px width with a negative right margin, so the cards spill off the right edge, overlap one another, and get clipped instead of flowing into a clean responsive grid; the active discipline tab is styled with near-black text on a near-identical dark chip so you cannot tell which discipline is selected. CROSS-ROUTE: the project browser must be present on the home, resume, and pursuits routes; wiring it into only the home surface leaves the resume and pursuits routes missing the shared browser. INTERACTION: clicking a discipline tab must actually re-filter the cards and update the live count — selecting "Web" must re-render the grid to the two Web projects and make the readout read "Showing 2 of 6 · Web"; a wiring bug that moves the active-tab highlight but snapshots the filtered set and readout at mount (so the grid keeps showing all six cards and the readout stays frozen on "Showing all 6 projects") is a stale-state regression. Repair the project browser so the tab row wraps and the filtered grid flows responsively with no horizontal overflow beyond the site's small pre-existing tolerance, the active tab is legibly highlighted, the discipline filter re-renders the cards and updates the live count, and the browser is present on all three primary routes — while keeping the portfolio's flat slate house style and the desktop/tablet appearance intact. The fix must be a genuine layout repair (let the tab row wrap and the card grid flow) and a genuine wiring repair (re-derive the filtered set and count from the selected discipline), not a cosmetic patch (narrowing a fixed width or clipping with overflow-x:hidden still leaves the document overflowing on mobile, and re-highlighting the tab without re-filtering leaves the count stale).
required_content: The 390px mobile Projects/contact states have no horizontal overflow beyond the site's small pre-existing tolerance; the document width tracks the 390px viewport instead of the tab row's fixed width.
The "Featured work" project browser shows its discipline tabs (All / Mobile / AI · ML / Web / Systems) and a live result count on the portfolio's flat slate tiles, on every viewport.
The filtered card grid flows into a clean responsive grid (cards no longer overlap, clip, or spill off the edge) and the active discipline tab is legibly highlighted.

The discipline filter stays live: selecting "Web" re-renders the grid to the two Web projects and updates the readout to "Showing 2 of 6 · Web" (the count and cards track the selected discipline, not a stale mount-time snapshot).
The shared project browser (discipline tab row + count readout) is present on all three primary routes — the home page and the /resume and /pursuits routes.

Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts of the project browser and the surrounding Projects section are preserved and continue to fit within the centered content column without introducing overflow.
The intro/hero, Top Skills grid, Projects grid, Experience timeline, and Connect contact form all remain reachable and render their headings and content across the captured states.
design_constraints: Preserve the portfolio's visual language: dark slate background, centered max-w-[1000px] column, Tailwind spacing rhythm, flat rounded slate tiles, and the amber accent used for the active-nav pill. Style the active discipline tab legibly (on-brand amber fill, dark text) rather than dark-on-dark.

Do not remove, rename, or reword the discipline tabs, the projects, or the count readout copy; the repair is about responsive reflow of the tab row + filtered grid, legible tab state, and live filter wiring.
Keep the desktop and tablet appearance of the project browser visually equivalent to a single fitted tab row over a clean card grid within the content column.

Fix the overflow at its source in the tab row's flex layout (allow wrapping) and the filtered grid's layout (let cards flow / wrap) rather than clipping the document or a container with overflow-x:hidden, which hides the symptom but leaves the layout broken.
Keep the discipline filter's count + card grid bound to the live selected discipline, and keep the shared project browser wired into every primary route (home / resume / pursuits).
Do not alter unrelated components, the fixed navbar, the contact form behavior, or the site's fonts and color palette.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and tablet_initial capture the top of the portfolio (fixed navbar + Alex Ross intro/hero); the layout fits the viewport with no horizontal overflow on desktop or tablet.
mobile_initial captures the 390px hero above the project browser; because the fixed-width tab row sits in the same document, the unrepaired build already shows the tab-row-induced overflow here.

desktop_skills, desktop_projects, and desktop_projects_lower capture the Top Skills grid and the Projects section (including the "Featured work" discipline filter and the project cards); on desktop the browser fits the content column with a clean card grid and keeps the flat slate tile styling.
desktop_experience and desktop_contact capture the Experience timeline and the Connect contact form; both fit the desktop content column.

mobile_projects and mobile_projects_lower capture the Projects section at 390px where the fixed-width no-wrap discipline tab row forces the document wider than the viewport, producing a large horizontal overflow in the unrepaired build.
mobile_contact captures the Connect form at 390px; the project browser above it in the same document still shows the tab-row-induced horizontal overflow in the unrepaired build.

desktop_filter_web scrolls to the project browser and clicks the "Web" discipline tab; the grid must then re-render to the two Web projects and the live readout must read "Showing 2 of 6 · Web" (a stale-state build leaves the grid on all six cards and the readout on "Showing all 6 projects").

desktop_home_browser, desktop_resume, and desktop_pursuits scroll to the shared project browser on the home / resume / pursuits routes; the browser's discipline tabs and count readout must be present on all three routes.
mobile_resume captures the /resume route at 390px; it fits the phone width with no horizontal overflow.

Source inspection confirms the tab row + filtered grid layout lives in app/components/proj-browser.css, the filter wiring in app/components/proj-browser.tsx, and the cross-route browser presence in app/lib/filter-routes.ts (consumed by app/components/proj-browser-mount.tsx).

change_completion: The 390px mobile Projects and contact states no longer overflow horizontally beyond the small pre-existing tolerance.

The discipline tab row wraps and the filtered card grid flows responsively (cards no longer overlap or clip) so the browser fits the phone width, and the discipline filter re-renders the cards and updates the live count from the selected discipline.
The discipline tabs, projects, and count readout remain present on every viewport, and the shared project browser is present on the home, resume, and pursuits routes.
design_consistency: Desktop and tablet keep a single fitted discipline tab row over a clean card grid within the centered content column.
The browser's flat slate tiles, spacing, typography, and the amber active-tab accent are preserved (no dark-on-dark illegible tab, no overlapping/clipped card grid).
No content, headings, or navigation are changed by the repair.
regression: The intro, skills, projects, experience, and contact sections all remain reachable and render their headings.
The fixed navbar, contact form, fonts, palette, and the shared project browser are unchanged.
responsive: 390px Projects/contact states have no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) states remain overflow-free with the project browser intact.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 14 App Router portfolio; capability=Repair, design_continuity, layout scope. The single well-scoped defect is a fixed-width, no-wrap career-metrics strip that overflows the document on 390px mobile while fitting desktop/tablet. Content and DOM are byte-identical across reference/baseline/bad legs; the sole discriminator is the no_horizontal_overflow gate (tolerance 24px) on the mobile Projects/contact states plus the console-error and DOM-assertion gates that hold on all legs. The reference repairs the strip with flex-wrap + flexible tiles; the baseline is the original-with-defect; the negative-control bad solution only narrows the fixed row and adds overflow-x:hidden, so the document still overflows.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Next.js 14 App Router software-engineer portfolio (Alex Ross) with a fixed navbar, intro, skills grid, projects section, experience timeline, and contact form, plus /resume and /pursuits routes; used for a design_continuity layout repair on the portfolio's own project browser — fixing a 390px mobile horizontal-overflow defect in a fixed-width discipline tab row, a broken/overlapping filtered card grid, an illegible active tab, and a stale discipline-filter count, while preserving the browser's slate styling, its live count readout, its cross-route presence, and the desktop/tablet layout.
